title: This lint checks for function arguments of type &String, &Vec, &PathBuf, and Cow<_>.
summary: It will also suggest you replace .clone() calls with the appropriate .to_owned()/to_string() calls. Requiring the argument to be of the specific type makes the function less useful for no benefit; slices in the form of &[T] or &str usually suffice and can be obtained from other types, too. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for as casts between raw pointers that don’t change their constness, namely *const T to *const U and *mut T to *mut U.
summary: Though as casts between raw pointers are not terrible, pointer::cast is safer because it cannot accidentally change the pointer’s mutability, nor cast the pointer to other types like usize. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for as casts between raw pointers that change their constness, namely *const T to *mut T and *mut T to *const T.
summary: Though as casts between raw pointers are not terrible, pointer::cast_mut and pointer::cast_const are safer because they cannot accidentally cast the pointer to another type. Or, when null pointers are involved, null() and null_mut() can be used directly. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Use std::ptr::eq when applicable
summary: ptr::eq can be used to compare &T references (which coerce to *const T implicitly) by their address rather than comparing the values they point to. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of the offset pointer method with an integer literal.
summary: The add and sub methods more accurately express the intent. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for usage of the offset pointer method with a usize cast to an isize.
summary: If we’re always increasing the pointer address, we can avoid the numeric cast by using the add method instead. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.
